findings.title: Protocol/transport-error failure mode has no test, though the design requires one
findings.description: The slice design's failure-mode table has a row for "Protocol/transport error mid-call (`McpError`, closed stream) → `is_error=True` + `logger.warning`" and states "Each row above has a test asserting the observable signal." Task 4.3 implements that handling, but Task 5's test list (echo, fail, empty, unknown-tool, timeout, spawn-failure) covers only the spawn/timeout/server-isError/missing-arg rows — there is no case driving a mid-call `McpError`/closed-stream and asserting the WARNING. The fake server (Task 3.1) also has no tool that can induce such a fault, so the fixture cannot support it. Add a fixture capability and a test for this row.

findings.title: Non-text-block result mapping is implemented but never verified
findings.description: The design's Result mapping rules require "Non-text blocks are noted by type in the content, not dropped silently." Task 4.2 implements it, but no test asserts it, and the fake server's `echo`/`empty` tools only produce text (or zero) blocks. Given the design's explicit "no silent no-op" emphasis, a fake-server tool that returns a mixed text/non-text result plus an assertion on the noted-by-type content would close the loop; as written this behavior is unverified.

findings.title: SC6's model-driven `cf_build_context` demo has no owning task
findings.description: SC6 requires that "a dispatch with a tool-capable non-SDK model can call `cf_build_context` and receive assembled context (walkthrough §4)." The first half (materialized `cf_workflow_status` returning real status) is covered by Tasks 8.2/9.1 step 2, but the end-to-end dispatch-with-model half is not: Task 9.1 runs only walkthrough steps 1–3, and Task 9.3 explicitly notes step 4 "remains open alongside 263's demo." No task schedules that demo. The standard-terminal constraint is real, but the success criterion is left unmet at slice close-out; a dedicated step-4 demo task (run outside Claude Code) should own it.
